transcript.customer: Show me fabric types for a warm neutral room with oak floors and olive-green furniture.

advice.text:
With oak floors and olive-green furniture, I’d start with warm neutrals that soften the scheme without turning yellow:

• Oatmeal linen-look: relaxed and softly textured, bridging the oak and olive.
• Warm stone herringbone: a more tailored option, with subtle pattern rather than a strong motif.
• Cream textured weave: a lighter contrast that lets the olive furniture stand out.

For a richer alternative, muted terracotta would bring warmth and more colour contrast. My fabric knowledge search returned no matches, so these are design directions rather than verified products.

Would you prefer an airy feel or something more cocooning?
advice.patternDirection: Plain or subtle herringbone, allowing the olive furniture to remain a focal point.
advice.textureDirection: Linen-look or softly textured weave; herringbone for a more tailored finish.
alternatives: Muted terracotta for a richer, contrasting direction rather than a neutral scheme.
questions: Would you prefer an airy feel or something more cocooning?

transcript.customer: The furniture will stay. I want the curtains softer and lighter, but not a stark white.

advice.text:
Then I’d favour a light oatmeal or soft ivory with a muted beige undertone, rather than brilliant white or yellow cream. Against the olive furniture, either could feel gently lighter while relating to the warmth of the oak.

A fine linen-look weave would give the curtains a soft, relaxed appearance without adding busy pattern. If oatmeal feels too brown, pale warm stone is a quieter alternative, though it may look cooler in limited daylight.
palette: Soft ivory with a muted beige undertone
advice.textureDirection: Fine linen-look weave with gentle, subtle texture.
alternatives: Pale warm stone for a less brown neutral, with the tradeoff that it may appear cooler in limited daylight.

For your room, I’d still favour light oatmeal with a fine, low-contrast weave: softer than stark white, with enough texture to sit comfortably beside oak and olive. Soft ivory is a lighter alternative. We could broaden the search by removing the colour restriction, then assess the returned shades separately.
